findings.reason: the plan's own §4 warns that a channel indistinguishable from silence is the defect being removed, yet the dispatched node's gate cannot distinguish a delivered message from an unread inbox.
findings.text: §7's done-when ("the worker read contract and the coordinator-side writer land and the two held ledger runs reconcile") carries no negative control and no measure that a written message is actually read by a working worker; the discriminating half ("a run that received none says so rather than being silent") lives only in §4's prose, and §4 has no `data-reckon` section record, so the node a coordinator would dispatch can close with the contracts landable and delivery never shown

findings.reason: one verdict cannot close both halves, and the external ledger repairs can hold a finished, verified inbox open indefinitely.
findings.text: §7 bundles three independent deliverables: the worker read contract (`reckon/crew/prompts.py`), the coordinator-side writer (CLI), and reconciling two ledger rows whose blocking defects are in the promotion surface and owned elsewhere; the ledger half builds nothing this plan designs, and the plan's own text says each row waits on a *separate* defect

findings.reason: an implementable status with undeclared upstream work is exactly the case the queue's declared-wait ordering exists to prevent; without it the node launches and collides.
findings.text: §7 is declared `data-status="implementable"` while its body states both halves are blocked on modules held by other runs and that two ledger rows wait on repairs dispatched elsewhere; the plan declares no `depends-on` and no section-level wait, so a coordinator dispatching from the roadmap will start work into two files another run holds

findings.reason: one of the two stated blockers is already gone, so a builder either waits on nothing or re-derives the claim, and the section reads as more blocked than it is.
findings.text: the section claims the coordinator-side writer "needs the CLI module, held by this plan's own unreconciled guard run", but the plan's own §3 comment (plan.html:259) records that run (`r-20260915T061057147322`) as reconciled by a later session on 2026-09-15, with its stale claim on `reckon/cli.py` released; no live pointer for it exists under `~/.config/reckon/crew/live/`

findings.reason: the builder must invent a CLI surface the plan treats as settled, and the guard's promise to a refused coordinator stays unfulfillable until that verb is named.
findings.text: neither §4 nor §7 names the command or module entry point of the coordinator-side writer; §3's landed guard (`reckon/hooks/worker_message_guard.py`, `RESUME_INVOCATION_SHAPE`) tells a refused coordinator the working channel for a *live* run is "the inbox of §4", so the plan's own shipped refusal points at an interface the plan never specifies

findings.reason: the anchor is a historical run comment whose claimed string resolves verbatim in the current tree, so no builder's action changes; the claim it supports ("resume refuses a live run") still holds.
findings.text: the run comment cites `runs.py:2081-2089` for the live-process refusal; that file/line pair now holds unrelated drain statistics, and the quoted string sits at `reckon/crew/resumption.py:1000`
